purpose: Reusable mechanics from elite signature interaction references. Extract mechanics, not brands.

patterns.name: Kinetic Poster Board
patterns.whatItDoes: Turns the page into a physical poster/work board where type, frames, rail navigation, and character punctuation carry memory.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for playful studios, agencies, culture, entertainment, and brand sites that can carry comedic scale.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for dashboards, forms, utilities, or dense reading flows.
patterns.interactionStory: The user travels across a board instead of scrolling through normal sections.
patterns.motionPattern: Type, cards, and mascot move as physical objects tied to scroll or route position.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use CSS grid/transform sections; GSAP ScrollTrigger is optional for pinned or horizontal travel.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Provide normal vertical reading order, skip links, and keyboard access.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Disable scrubbed travel and show stacked poster sections.
scoreCaps: generic section stack after signature refs: max 4
no reduced-motion fallback: max 5

patterns.name: Scroll Route Choreography
patterns.whatItDoes: Maps content to a memorable route instead of a vertical section stack.
patterns.whenToUse: Use when content can be experienced as a map, route, timeline, reel, board, or spatial story.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when SEO reading, accessibility-critical access, or form completion is primary.
patterns.interactionStory: The user moves horizontally, vertically, or through territory changes with intention.
patterns.motionPattern: Pinned or snap sections move along a route; motion always reflects the route map.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use CSS scroll-snap for simple routes; use GSAP ScrollTrigger only when scrubbed/pinned precision is needed.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Expose all content in DOM order and provide route landmarks.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Collapse to a normal vertical stack.
scoreCaps: route claim but fade/slide delivered: max 4

patterns.name: Floating Product Ingredient Stage
patterns.whatItDoes: Makes product and ingredient objects feel physical, layered, and ownable.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for tangible products, food, beverage, commerce, beauty, hardware, and object-led brands.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for abstract SaaS unless truthful product objects exist.
patterns.interactionStory: The user sees the product world assemble around real objects and ingredients.
patterns.motionPattern: Subtle depth drift, rotation, or scroll parallax by layer.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use layered SVG/images with transforms; every object needs a role and alt/fallback.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Show a static product object with ordered ingredient descriptions.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Remove floating motion and show the ordered ingredient panel.
scoreCaps: object motion decorative only: max 6
product objects are fake or unsupported: max 5

patterns.name: Scroll-to-Assemble Cards
patterns.whatItDoes: Transforms scattered content into an organized set as the user scrolls.
patterns.whenToUse: Use when the product value is organizing chaos, ingredients, evidence, reviews, artifacts, or steps.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid if cards are ordinary feature blocks with no before/after logic.
patterns.interactionStory: The user watches disorder become a system.
patterns.motionPattern: Cards translate/rotate from scattered positions into a grid/list or labeled stack.
patterns.implementationNotes: Keep accessible order in DOM; transforms are progressive enhancement.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Show ordered cards by default with optional before-state copy.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Skip scattered state and reveal organized stack.
scoreCaps: random scroll effects: max 5
no reduced-motion fallback: max 5

patterns.name: Review Theater Cards
patterns.whatItDoes: Turns reviews/testimonials into branded artifacts instead of generic quote grids.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for brands with strong voice and real testimonials or social proof.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid fake reviews, regulated proof claims, or generic B2B quote grids.
patterns.interactionStory: The user browses reviews as physical labels, tickets, or stage cards.
patterns.motionPattern: Cards slide, snap, fan, stack, or stage as a row.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use real source metadata and accessible list/card semantics.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Readable list of reviews with source labels.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Static cards in list or accessible carousel.
scoreCaps: generic reviews despite Review Theater pattern: max 6

patterns.name: Editorial List Detail Modal
patterns.whatItDoes: Makes list rows into navigational objects that open a designed information panel.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for editorial tech, feature indexes, sectors, FAQs, process lists, and structured discovery.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when the modal is only a default dialog or content dump.
patterns.interactionStory: The user scans a confident index, then opens a rich panel without leaving the editorial system.
patterns.motionPattern: Panel opens with restrained slide/scale while selected row remains legible.
patterns.implementationNotes: Rows are buttons; panel uses product typography, tokens, focus trap, and Escape close.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Focus trap, Escape close, aria-modal or inline accordion, return focus to row.
scoreCaps: modal/detail interaction uses default dialog styling: max 6

patterns.name: Portal Object Entry
patterns.whatItDoes: Uses a tiny object, crack, or mark as an entry portal into the site world.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for portfolios, studios, campaigns, cinematic launches, and object-led editorial pages.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for high-frequency utility tasks or pages needing immediate forms.
patterns.interactionStory: The user is drawn into a small object and rewarded with media or work behind it.
patterns.motionPattern: Slow scale/camera move into shape; media appears inside or behind the portal.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use CSS clip-path or SVG mask; fake portal claims without mask/scale implementation fail.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Provide direct content links and readable alt text.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Show static hero media plus direct content grid.
commonFailureSigns: fake portal claim with fade only
scoreCaps: portal/morphing claim but only fade/slide delivered: max 4

patterns.name: Media Constellation Stage
patterns.whatItDoes: Arranges media/work items as a spatial constellation instead of equal cards.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for portfolios, case studies, reels, and media-heavy brand work.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for dense admin, equal-priority catalogs, or small data sets with no media richness.
patterns.interactionStory: The user discovers work as spatial rewards around a cinematic stage.
patterns.motionPattern: Media drifts/reveals subtly; hover/focus clarifies the selected item.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use positioned CSS grid/canvas only when keyboard order and responsive fallback are defined.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Provide list view and keyboard order matching visual order.
scoreCaps: media collage with no interaction model: max 6

patterns.name: Playful Entry Gate
patterns.whatItDoes: Makes entry into the site a small memorable action.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for playful brand sites where ceremony is part of the promise.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for accessibility-critical, emergency, utility, dashboard, or conversion-sensitive flows.
patterns.interactionStory: The user performs a tiny ritual before entering, while a skip path preserves access.
patterns.motionPattern: Bounce, throw, click, or unlock motion transitions into the site.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use local state and simple CSS transforms; never require physics precision.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Skip button and keyboard activation are required.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Skip gate and show site content.
scoreCaps: playful interaction blocks access with no fallback: max 5

patterns.name: Mascot Hero Interaction
patterns.whatItDoes: Lets a custom mascot or character carry the main memory of the page.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for brands where a character can carry identity and tone.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid generic mascot injection into serious products.
patterns.interactionStory: The user remembers the page through the character's position, motion, and relationship to type.
patterns.motionPattern: Slow idle motion with small hover/click response; never busy.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use inline SVG or optimized image; mascot needs role, bounds, and text-safe zones.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Static mascot with descriptive alt text or decorative hiding when appropriate.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Static mascot with no idle movement.
scoreCaps: mascot pasted in without role: max 6
amateur illustration: max 4

patterns.name: Directional Page Transition
patterns.whatItDoes: Makes route changes feel directional and place-like.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for brand, service, portfolio, or editorial sites with a small route set.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid complex apps where route changes must be instant and predictable.
patterns.interactionStory: The user feels they move to a new room or destination, not just load a page.
patterns.motionPattern: Page enters from right/left/top with color or material shift.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use CSS transitions between route containers and restore focus to the heading.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Respect browser history and focus target heading.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Instant route change with color/state only.
scoreCaps: route transition blocks content: max 6

patterns.name: Service Ritual Selector
patterns.whatItDoes: Turns service selection into a focused ritual instead of a generic form.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for booking, intake, configurators, or service selection where focus and brand tone matter.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when users need fast comparison tables or high-frequency repeated task entry.
patterns.interactionStory: The user makes one deliberate choice at a time and sees the service world respond.
patterns.motionPattern: Short directional step transitions with clear state and no delay.
patterns.implementationNotes: Build as accessible stepper/select flow with large type and clear affordances.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: All fields accessible with labels and error messages.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Show standard form/list with the same data.
scoreCaps: ritual blocks task: max 5

patterns.name: Annotation Ritual
patterns.sourceInspiration: Nocturne correction pattern from field guide failure
patterns.whatItDoes: Reveals a specimen through draw-on annotations, protected labels, stamps, and collector notes.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for field guides, archives, botanical/specimen pages, technical product anatomy, or editorial evidence reveals.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when labels are decorative only or cannot be protected from illustration paths.
patterns.interactionStory: The user watches the specimen become legible through staged annotation instead of static labels.
patterns.motionPattern: Lines draw from anchors to protected label boxes; stamps/notes appear after the line settles.
patterns.implementationNotes: Never use child SVG title tooltips; leader lines must route around labels and text.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Provide ordered annotation list tied to specimen regions.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Show all labels and notes statically with line drawing disabled.
scoreCaps: leader line cuts word: max 3
native SVG tooltip visible: max 4
static SVG where animated reveal is required: max 5

patterns.name: Specimen Lens Entry
patterns.sourceInspiration: Nocturne correction pattern from field guide failure
patterns.whatItDoes: Uses a tiny lens, seed, moon mark, or specimen dot as the entry object that opens into the field guide.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for botanical, scent, archive, field guide, museum, or evidence-led landing pages.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when the object cannot be implemented as a real mask/scale/entry state.
patterns.interactionStory: The user enters through a small mark and discovers the specimen world inside it.
patterns.motionPattern: Click or scroll expands the mark into a lens/mask that reveals the guide.
patterns.implementationNotes: Use CSS clip-path, SVG mask, or scale transform; do not claim portal/lens with fade only.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Provide direct link to the field guide content.
patterns.reducedMotionFallback: Show the lens mark and guide content statically.
commonFailureSigns: lens is only a decorative circle
scoreCaps: portal/lens claim but only fade/slide delivered: max 4
no fallback: max 5

patterns.name: Field Guide Plate Drawer
patterns.sourceInspiration: Nocturne correction pattern from field guide failure
patterns.whatItDoes: Turns specimen plates from scattered or stacked artifacts into an organized archival guide.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for field guides, collections, catalogs, editorial archives, cards, specimens, ingredients, or evidence sets.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when plates are ordinary content cards with no archival or organization story.
patterns.interactionStory: The user sees the collection become usable as plates file into an archival drawer.
patterns.motionPattern: Scroll or click moves plates from offset stack into drawer/list positions.
patterns.implementationNotes: Keep DOM order logical; transforms are decoration over accessible plate list.
patterns.accessibilityFallback: Provide ordered plate list with headings and details.
scoreCaps: static SVG where animated reveal is required: max 5
random scroll effects: max 5
